subject: Confirmatory Factor Analysis with multilevel data (not growth curve)

messages.author: 2f4d5569c4d39a58
messages.subject: Confirmatory Factor Analysis with multilevel data (not growth curve)
parts:
Hi, I am trying to perform Confirmatory Factor Analysis on a data set with a nested design. I want to be able to include the equivalent of random intercepts that I would if I were using HLM in order to control for error associated with the nested design. I am having trouble understanding how to do this in lavaan. 

In my data users took part of an experiment in three-person groups. After the experiment they filled out a questionnaire. I am performing CFA to test the fit of a particular factor structure on the questionnaire and I want to do so at the individual level. However, I also want to be able to control for the fact that users took part in the experiment in groups (which may have introduced random error). My data looks something like this:

User | Group | Item 1 | Item 2 | Item 3 ...
u1 | g1 | 8 | 4 | 4 ...
u2 | g1 | 4 | 2 | 3 ...
u3 | g1 | 9 | 2 | 5 ...
u4 | g2 | 3 | 2 | 5 ...

There are two types of examples that I've seen that might apply, but neither seems quite right. One, I could perform a comparison of the factor structure across groups keeping most things constant (essentially treating the groups as independent samples). I don't think this would be right because my groups are very small n=3, I'm not really interested in how the model is different across groups, and they aren't exactly different samples. Two, I could represent random intercepts as latent factors as is done in growth curves. This would require me to reformat the data into a wide format (u1,u2,u3) and does not seem right because I would have to group users arbitrarily into columns. Unlike typical longitudinal or repeated measures data, there in no meaning to being the first person in a group like there is being the first measurement. Is there a way to make one of these approaches work? Or is there an alternative?

Thanks in advance for any guidance you may be able to provide.

Yla

Have a look at the lavaan.survey package. You can treat 'group' as a
clustering variable, and get a 'robust' solution taking the
cluster-effect into account.

Alternatively, since you only have three subjects within each group,
would it be unreasonable to average the results (of the three subjects)
and do an analysis with groups as units?

Yves.
